Rashi on Pesachim 50b:10:2.hebrew: אינן רואין - כדאמרן, שאם יתעשרו לא יהו עסוקין:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:10:2.english: They do not see - As we said, for if they become wealthy, they will not be engaged [in this work].

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:10:3.english: And if they engage [in it] for its own sake - So that the mitzvah be available to those who need it.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:10:4.hebrew: רואין - דהואיל ולשמה עושין, לא יניחו בשביל עשרן:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:10:4.english: They see [blessing] - For since they do [so] for its own sake, they will not abandon [their work] because of their wealth.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:11:1.hebrew: מצור לצידון - יום השוק של צידון בע"ש, והם מחמירים על עצמן שלא להיבטל מצרכי שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:11:1.english: From Tyre to Sidon - [It was] the market day of Sidon on Shabbat eve, and they were stringent upon themselves so as not to be kept from Shabbat needs.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:11:2.hebrew: הוה אפשר להו - להמנע מן השוק, שעשירים היו:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:11:2.english: It was possible for them - to refrain from [going to] the market, for they were wealthy.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:1:1.hebrew: ואל ישנה אדם - בגמרא פריך: ממקום שאין עושין למקום שעושין, ואיהו נמי אל ישנה וליעבד? והא אמרת: נותנין עליו חומרי מקום שיצא משם:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:1:1.english: And a person may not deviate - In the Gemara, it asks: [When going] from a place where they do not do [work] to a place where they do [work], should he too not deviate and do [work]? But didn't you say [that] we place upon him the stringencies of the place from which he departed?

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:1:2.hebrew: המוליך פירות שביעית ממקום שכלו - לחיה מן השדה, וחייבין בני המקום לבערן מן הבית, והוליכן זה למקום שלא כלו, ובני אותו מקום עדיין אוכלין הכנוסין בבית:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:1:2.english: One who transports Sabbatical [Year] produce from a place where they have ceased - for the wild beast from the field, and the residents of the place are obligated to remove them from the house, and this [person] transported them to a place where they have not ceased, and the residents of that place are still eating what is gathered in the house.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:1:3.english: [He] is obligated to remove [them] - Because of the stringencies of the place from which he departed.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:1:4.english: Go out and bring for yourself, you too - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:2:1.hebrew: מאי איריא ערבי פסחים - דקתני עד חצות במנהגא, מכלל דמחצות ולהלן אסור. ולמה ליה למיתני חצות לאשמעינן הך דיוקא? הא כל ערבי ימים טובים אסירי:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:2:1.english: Why [teach] particularly Passover eves - For [the Mishnah] taught "until midday" [as dependent] on custom, which implies that from midday onward it is prohibited. And why did [the Tanna] need to teach "midday" to inform us of this inference? Behold, all Festival eves are prohibited.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:2:2.english: From mincha - Nine and a half hours [into the day].

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:3:1.english: A trace of sin - A hint of sin.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:3:2.hebrew: תענית צבור - אסור במלאכה במסכת תענית (דף יב:) כשהיו מתענין על הגשמים, אבל שאר תענית ציבור לא, כדאמר שמואל: אין חומר תענית ציבור בבבל (לקמן פסחים דף נד:):
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:3:2.english: A communal fast - [Labor] is prohibited [on it], [as taught] in Tractate Taanit (12b) when they would fast for rain; however, [on] other communal fasts, [it is] not [prohibited], as Shmuel said: There is no stringency of a communal fast in Babylonia (below, Pesachim 54b).

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:3:3.english: On the conclusions of Shabbat - Because of the honor of Shabbat, as we add from the mundane to the sacred.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:4:2.hebrew: שפל ונשכר דלא עביד כולה שבתא ולא במעלי שבתא - ואע"ג דלאו לשום מצוה מיכוין, מצוה שלא לשמה מיהא הויא, דאמרינן לקמן: יעסוק אדם במצוה ואפילו שלא לשמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:4:2.english: Lazy and rewarded, [which is] one who does not work the entire week and not on Shabbat eve - Even though he does not intend [it] for the sake of a mitzvah, it is nevertheless a mitzvah [performed] not for its own sake, as we say later: "A person should engage in a mitzvah even not for its own sake."

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:4:3.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>, <abbr title="ואף על גב">ואע"ג</abbr> דהאי דלא קעבדן כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:4:3.english: We read thus: "And even though this [fact] that they do not work, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:4:4.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> <abbr title="ואף על גב">ואע"ג</abbr> דהאי דלא קעבדן כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:4:4.english: This is the reading: "And even though the fact that they do not work, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:5:1.hebrew: עושין לשמה - מעל שמים, ושלא לשמה עד לשמים, דמצוה מיהא קא עביד, כדרב יהודה:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:5:1.english: [Those who] perform [a mitzvah] for its own sake - [God's mercy is] above the heavens, and [for those who perform it] not for its own sake, [it is] unto the heavens, since he is at least performing a mitzvah, in accordance with [the statement of] Rav Yehuda.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:6:1.hebrew: מתקולתא - נוטלת מאזנים בידה ומהלכת בשוק להשכירן לכל הצריכין, דשכר מועט הוא ומתבזה אשתו על שכר מועט:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:6:1.english: Matkulta [a scale] - [She] takes scales in her hand and walks in the marketplace to rent them out to all who need [them], for it is a meager wage, and his wife is demeaned for a meager wage.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:6:2.hebrew: אגרתא - שכר ריחיים שמשכירין, טורח גדול ושכר מועט. אבל קונה ריחיים ומוכרן, הרי הוא כשאר פרקמטיא:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:6:2.english: Rent - The rental fee of a mill that one rents out [involves] great exertion and little profit. However, [if] one buys mills and sells them, it is like any other merchandise.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:1.hebrew: בקנים - כל מקלות דקים קרי קנים, שעושין מהן גדרות ומחיצות:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:1.english: With reeds - All thin sticks are called reeds, from which they make fences and partitions.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:3.hebrew: תגרי סימטא - יושבין ומוכרין בשוק, ועין שולטת בהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:3.english: Merchants of an alleyway [simta] - [They] sit and sell in the marketplace, and the [evil] eye dominates them.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:4.english: And those who raise small livestock - Everyone cries out against them.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:5.hebrew: וקוצצי אילנות טובות - למוכרן לעצים, הכל תמיהים ומלעיזין עליהם, ומתוך כך עין שולטת בהן וצעקת בני אדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:5.english: And those who chop down good trees - [That is,] to sell them for wood; everyone wonders and scoffs at them, and consequently the [evil] eye and the outcry of people dominate them.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:6.hebrew: ונותנין עיניהם בחלק יפה - כשחולקים עם אחרים, תמיד מקפידין ליטול חלק יפה:
Rashi on Pesachim 50b:7:6.english: And those who set their eyes on the fine portion - When they divide [something] with others, they are always particular to take a fine portion.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:8:1.english: Interpreters - Who stand before the sage on Sabbaths, hear from his mouth, and announce [it] to the public.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:9:1.english: And orphans' money - [invested] for half the profit.

Rashi on Pesachim 50b:9:2.english: From a country overseas - [He] constantly sends his ships to a place of danger.

Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:10:1.hebrew: כותבי ספרים - אור"י בשם ריב"א, דדוקא הכותבים כדי למכור, עליהן בקשו — דלעולם ימצאו לוקחין, כדקתני "הן ותגריהם"; אבל על המשכירים עצמן לבעלי בתים לא בקשו, שלא היו מקפחים פרנסתן, שלא ימצאו כל כך להשתכר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:10:1.english: Scribes [who write] scrolls - Ri says in the name of Riva that specifically [regarding] those who write in order to sell, about them they prayed [that they not become wealthy], for they will always find buyers, as [the baraita] teaches: "they and their merchants"; however, regarding those who hire themselves out to householders, they did not pray [thus], for they would not impair their livelihood [such] that they would not find enough to earn a living.

Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:2:1.hebrew: העושה מלאכה במוצאי שבתות - אור"י דאיתא בירושלמי הכי: "הני נשי דנהיגי דלא למעבד עבידתא באפוקי שבתא — לאו מנהגא; עד דתיתפני סידרא — מנהגא". פי': שישלים התפלה — מנהג כשר, ובהא איירי נמי הכא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:2:1.english: One who performs labor at the close of Shabbat - Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that it is stated in the Yerushalmi thus: "Those women who have the custom not to do work at the close of Shabbat — [this is] not a [binding] custom; until the order [of prayers] is concluded — [this is] a [valid] custom." Explanation: [waiting] until one completes the prayer is a proper custom, and it is this [case] that [the Gemara] is also discussing here.

Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:5:1.hebrew: וכאן בעושים שלא לשמה וכדרב יהודה - תימה, (דרב) גופיה אמר בפ"ב דברכות (ד' יז.): "כל העוסק בתורה שלא לשמה, נוח לו שלא נברא". ואור"י, דהתם מיירי כגון שלומד כדי להתיהר ולקנטר ולקפח את חביריו בהלכה, ואינו לומד ע"מ לעשות. אבל הכא מיירי דומיא דההיא דלעיל: "יש שפל ונשכר, דלא עביד כוליה שבתא ולא במעלי שבתא", שאין מתכוון לשום רעה אלא מתוך עצלות; אפ"ה "גדול עד שמים חסדו":
Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:5:1.english: "And here, [when] they perform [a mitzva] not for its own sake, and [this is] in accordance with [the statement of] Rav Yehuda" - This is astonishing, [for] (Rav) himself said in the second chapter of Berakhot (17a): "Anyone who engages in Torah [study] not for its own sake, it would have been better for him had he not been created"! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that there it is referring to a case such as where one studies in order to boast, to vex, and to best his colleagues in halakha, and does not study in order to practice [it]. However, here it is referring to a case similar to that [teaching] above: "There is [one who is] lazy and rewarded, who does not work the entire week and [does] not [work] on Shabbat eve" — for he has no evil intention, rather [he acts] out of laziness; even so, "His mercy is great unto the heavens."

Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:6:1.hebrew: מתקולתא - מטוה. לכך קורא אותה מתקולתא, לפי שנשכרת לשיעור משקל מטוה, כדתנן בכתובות (ד' סד:): "כמה היא עושה לו? משקל ה' סלעים". ופר"ח שהיא מתבזה על כך, שהיא מגלה זרועותיה בשעת טוויה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:6:1.english: Matkolta - [This refers to] spun thread. Therefore [the Gemara] calls it matkolta, because she is hired for a set weight of spun thread, as we learned in the Mishnah in Ketubot (64b): "How much must she make for him? The weight of five selaim." And Rabbeinu Chananel explained that she is demeaned by this, because she uncovers her arms while spinning:

Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:7:1.hebrew: ומגדלי בהמה - וקשה לר"ת, דאמר (בחולין ד' פד:): "הרוצה שיתעשר יעסוק בבהמה דקה", ואמר נמי: "עשתרות — שמעשרות את בעליהן". וי"ל דהתם בחורשין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 50b:7:1.english: And those who raise [small] livestock - And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, for [the Gemara] states (Chullin 84b): "One who wishes to become wealthy should engage in [raising] small livestock," and it also states: "Ashtarot — [meaning] that they enrich their owners." And one can answer that there [it refers to raising them] in forests.
